entries.name: Expectation Conditional Maximization
entries.definition: An extension of expectation maximization that replaces a joint maximization of the expected complete-data log likelihood with a sequence of constrained maximizations, holding the E-step expectation fixed throughout that sequence.
entries.identity_notes: The Meng-Rubin ECM framework allows general constraint functions; coordinate-block maximization is a special case. It is distinct from posterior Gibbs sampling, ECME steps on actual observed likelihood, and parameter-expanded EM. Ordinary EM is recovered by one unconstrained maximization. Multicycle ECM refreshes the expectation within an outer iteration and is identified here as a related schedule variant, not the fixed-Q definition. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels and scoped synonyms and 463 preceding native IDs, names and aliases. Fixed-string searches of worktree and main included ignored and hidden files, yielding 52 and 53 matched lines respectively. All 41 distinct contextual passages across 105 line instances and nine checkout-qualified paths were read; these concern prior discovery references and factor-analysis evidence, plus an unrelated ignored URI-template parameter-expansion string. They are not existing identities for these three algorithms. All 223 semantic label/synonym rows were read. Fifteen exact annotated AIO CLASS nodes and outgoing edges were inspected: fourteen verified unchanged after prior reading and DataAugmentation newly read. Twenty-five contextual YAMLs comprise fifteen AIO and ten native records; twenty are unchanged verified prior readings, two are hash-verified final records fully read in the preceding cohort, and three were fully read here. General EM, tempered EM, Gaussian factor models, PPCA mixtures, Gibbs/Metropolis sampling, specialized deep Bayesian data augmentation and alternating Newton fitting do not identify these particular conditional/expanded EM procedures. claims.statement: At theta_t compute Q(theta|theta_t), the conditional expectation of complete-data log likelihood given the observed data under theta_t. Starting at theta_t, CM step s maximizes that same Q subject to g_s(theta)=g_s(theta_previous_substep). The constraint preserves feasibility of the previous substep. Use the final CM result as theta_(t+1), then compute the next E step. The constraints can fix a parameter block, its complement, or a more general function; the CM subproblems need not have closed-form solutions.

evidence.locator: Sections 2-3, pp.269-273 / PDF pp.3-7, especially Equations 3.1-3.3

claims.statement: Exact CM steps make the fixed Q nondecreasing, so the full ECM iteration is a generalized EM step and makes observed likelihood nondecreasing. This compares the final iterate with the E-step anchor; it does not require observed likelihood to increase between every pair of intermediate CM points. Stationary-limit results additionally require the stated regularity and parameter-space coverage conditions. In the differentiable full-rank formulation, space filling requires that the available constraint-tangent directions collectively span the parameter directions.

evidence.locator: Sections 3-4, Equations 3.4-3.7, Theorems 1-3 and Corollary 1, pp.272-275 / PDF pp.6-9; curator Gaussian counterexample to intermediate observed-likelihood monotonicity

claims.statement: Incomplete normal-data examples use old conditional first and second moments throughout the CM sequence, while regression coefficients and covariance parameters change in their specified order. Missing values replaced only by conditional means discard required uncertainty terms. Multicycle ECM refreshes expectations before selected CM steps; its outer update need not increase one single original Q, although each valid refreshed cycle has its own EM ascent relation.

evidence.locator: Section 2 Example 1, pp.269-270 / PDF pp.3-4; Section 5, pp.276-277 / PDF pp.10-11

limitations: Bounded monotone likelihood values do not alone establish parameter convergence, stationarity, a local maximum or global optimality. The source stationary-limit theorems impose regularity, interior and space-filling conditions, with additional uniqueness or alternative technical conditions on CM updates.

Optimizing only a restricted set of directions can stop at a point with nonzero gradient in an excluded direction. Arbitrary approximate Newton or other numerical steps require their own ascent checks.
The framework is deterministic likelihood or specified posterior-mode optimization, not posterior simulation. The incomplete-data examples assume an appropriate ignorable missingness formulation.

CM simplicity, number of iterations and total computation are different considerations. The source does not supply a universal speed ordering among EM, ECM and multicycle ECM. Finite curator examples check scheduling and direction-coverage boundaries; no historical fit or author software was reproduced.

claims.statement: Compute the E-step expectation at the current parameter. Carry out the selected conditional Q maximizations using that fixed expectation, followed by the selected conditional actual-likelihood maximizations at the current intermediate parameters. The Q sequence establishes likelihood ascent relative to its E-step anchor; the subsequent observed-likelihood steps preserve or improve that value. The complete ECME iteration need not increase the original Q and therefore need not be a generalized EM step relative to that Q.

evidence.locator: Introduction, p.730 / PDF p.2; Section 3, pp.733-734 / PDF pp.5-6; curator Gaussian comparison of Q-then-likelihood and invalid stale-Q reverse ordering

claims.statement: For the multivariate t normal/gamma augmentation, compute expected latent weights from the old parameters. Update location and scatter through Q at the old degrees of freedom, then conditionally maximize actual observed likelihood over positive degrees of freedom using the new location and scatter. In this final step, terms depending on degrees of freedom must vary with each trial value; they are not frozen old E-step statistics. The fully observed scatter update centers weighted residuals at the new mean and divides by sample count. The parameter is scatter, not the marginal t covariance.

evidence.locator: Sections 2-6, pp.20-28 / PDF pp.2-10, especially Section 6 Equations 29-30; consistent sufficient-statistic expression in Equation 24

claims.statement: In the inspected Gaussian factor-analysis application, Q updates loadings and any free factor-covariance parameters, followed by actual-likelihood fitting of diagonal uniqueness variances at those updated values. Numerical Newton steps are acceptable only with the required likelihood increase; Newton iteration alone does not guarantee it. This changes the fitting procedure while retaining the same marginal factor model.

evidence.locator: Section 3, pp.733-734 / PDF pp.5-6

limitations: Observed-likelihood ascent is not global optimality or unconditional parameter convergence. Conditional numerical solves require valid parameter constraints and objective safeguards; a stationary root need not be the intended conditional maximum.

The scheduling statement is the final-likelihood-step construction supported by the inspected sources. An earlier likelihood update followed by an unrefreshed Q update can decrease the full-iteration likelihood, as the saved curator Gaussian example shows.

The t examples assume ignorable missingness and correct conditional first and second moments. The source contains inconsistent displayed conditional-mean signs and old/new mean subscripts; the record uses the model-consistent moment interpretation and does not reproduce those expressions.

The original 1994 publisher PDF returned HTTP 403. Its general rate proof is not claimed as read. Two complete primary follow-ups support the stated method; historical iteration/time comparisons, clinical examples and source software were not reproduced. No universal acceleration or compute-cost guarantee is asserted.

claims.statement: Specify an expanded complete-data density p_X(y_com|theta_star,alpha) that recovers the original augmentation at alpha_0 and whose observed density equals the original density at theta=R(theta_star,alpha). At each iteration embed the current theta with alpha_0, compute expanded conditional sufficient moments, maximize expanded Q over the expanded parameters, reduce by R, and reset the auxiliary parameter to alpha_0 for the next E step. The observed-density equality makes expanded EM ascent transfer to the original likelihood.

evidence.locator: Sections 3.1-3.2, Equations 3.1-3.2 and Theorem 1, pp.758-759 / PDF pp.5-6

claims.statement: For a p-dimensional t distribution with fixed positive degrees of freedom nu, old latent weights are w_i=(nu+p)/(nu+delta_i), with delta_i the old scatter-based squared Mahalanobis distance. Ordinary EM uses the weighted mean and scatter sum_i w_i(y_i-mu_new)(y_i-mu_new)^T/N. Expanding the mean of the latent gamma scale yields alpha_new=sum_i w_i/N. Dividing the expanded scatter by alpha_new reduces to the original t model, giving denominator sum_i w_i instead of N; the next iteration resets alpha to one. This normalization follows from the stated expansion and reduction.

evidence.locator: Section 2, pp.756-758 / PDF pp.3-5

claims.statement: For y|z~Normal(z,1), z~Normal(theta,sigma_squared), with known positive sigma_squared, ordinary EM updates theta to m=(theta_old+sigma_squared*y)/(1+sigma_squared). Expanding the conditional observation mean to z+alpha gives theta_star_new=m and alpha_new=y-m. The reduction theta_star+alpha returns theta_new=y in one iteration, while ordinary EM contracts its error by 1/(1+sigma_squared). This exact example does not establish one-step convergence for other expansions.

evidence.locator: Section 3.4, pp.761-762 / PDF pp.8-9; curator scalar arithmetic

claims.statement: The information-matrix comparison linearizes at a converged likelihood solution under the stated differentiability, invertibility and positive-information conditions. It orders the slowest local linear convergence direction relative to the parent EM and permits equality. The paper’s global rate terminology refers to the extremal local direction, not convergence from arbitrary initializations. It does not order every finite iterate or total computational time.

evidence.locator: Section 3.3, pp.760-761 / PDF pp.7-8; Section 5, pp.768-769 / PDF pp.15-16

limitations: Finding a useful likelihood-preserving expansion is problem-specific. Additional free observed-model parameters without a valid reduction do not constitute this PX-EM construction.

Monotone bounded likelihood values alone do not prove parameter convergence or global optimality. Approximate expanded maximization and matrix/scatter boundary cases need separate validity and ascent checks.

The probit second-moment expression printed on p.766 fails the zero-predictor half-normal check, and the Poisson latent-count expectation printed on p.768 conflicts with the stated Poisson split. These curator-identified discrepancies are retained in the ledger; the record does not assert those example formulas.

ecm.paper: Maximum likelihood estimation via the ECM algorithm: A general framework
ecm.version: Biometrika 80(2), 267-278 (1993); institution-hosted journal scan with 2016 download watermark
ecm.pagination: Printed page equals PDF page plus 266.
ecm.abstract_interpretation: A general deterministic likelihood-fitting framework replaces a difficult joint EM maximization with simpler constrained maximizations. The abstract emphasizes stable ascent and examples; later theorems impose conditions for stationary limit points, and the discussion denies a universal speed ordering.

mechanism.note: Q(theta|theta_old) is the old conditional expectation of complete-data log likelihood. Original ECM holds that expectation fixed through a sequence of constrained CM steps. A partition into coordinate blocks is a useful special case, not the entire definition. Constraints may fix a block, all other blocks, or more general functions.

mechanism.locator: Section3, Equations3.1-3.3 and Definition1, p.272 / PDF6
mechanism.note: At CM step s, maximize the same Q(theta|theta_t) subject to g_s(theta)=g_s(theta_previous_substep); the last intermediate parameter starts the next E step. S=1 with constant constraint gives ordinary EM. A constrained optimizer must actually maximize or, for a generalized variant, supply the appropriate ascent; an arbitrary numeric step is insufficient.

Space filling means feasible tangent directions from the constraint sets generate the full parameter direction space. Under differentiable full-rank constraint gradients, the intersection of their column spaces is zero. This is a condition on directions available across CM steps, not on sampling or coverage of data.

For normal Y_i with mean X_i beta and general covariance Sigma, fix old Sigma and update beta by weighted least squares; then use new beta for the residual covariance update. With missing values, use old conditional means AND second moments throughout this ECM iteration. Replacing YY transpose by only products of conditional means drops posterior uncertainty.

The no-three-way-interaction 2x2x2 contingency model uses a cycle of conditional probability-preserving two-way marginal updates. Start in the restricted model; a uniform table supplies one such start. With incomplete counts, expected margins replace observed ones. Conditional probability constraints vary across steps rather than fixing one universal coordinate partition.

Gamma shape/scale example updates scale as conditional mean divided by old shape, then solves the inverse-digamma shape equation using the new scale and expected log observations. ecme.abstract_interpretation: A primary method/application paper develops likelihood fitting for multivariate t distributions with known or unknown degrees of freedom, incomplete outcomes and linear predictors. It compares EM, multicycle ECM and ECME. Full text preserves nonconvexity and small-sample caveats; the abstract local-maximum wording is not an unconditional theorem.

mechanism.note: ECME replaces selected constrained expected-complete-log-likelihood CM steps with constrained actual-observed-log-likelihood steps. In the exhibited two-block schedule, compute old conditional moments, update location and scatter by Q at fixed old nu, then maximize actual likelihood over nu at the new location/scatter. This is generally not a GEM relative to one old Q. It is not unconstrained observed-likelihood maximization in every coordinate and not arbitrary mixing of stale Q and actual-likelihood updates.

The t model is a normal/gamma scale mixture: tau~Gamma(nu/2,rate nu/2), Y|tau~N(mu,Psi/tau). Psi is scatter, not the marginal covariance; covariance exists for nu>2 and equals nu/(nu-2)*Psi, while the mean requires nu>1. Expected latent weight for p_i observed coordinates is (nu+p_i)/(nu+delta_i). Missing responses require expected weighted cross-products, including conditional covariance rather than mean-only imputation.

Location is the weighted mean; scatter divides weighted residuals by n, with residuals around the new mean. Unknown nu EM uses expected log tau minus expected tau, not log of expected tau. The completed-data Q separates the (mu,Psi) block and nu, so basic ECM with that partition equals EM. Multicycle ECM refreshes the conditional moments after updating (mu,Psi) before fitting nu.

In the actual-likelihood nu step, weights and digamma terms depend on the trial nu; they are not frozen old expected sufficient statistics. A numerical solver must respect positive nu, possible normal-limit boundary and the intended conditional maximum/increase; arbitrary stationary roots do not constitute an unconditional optimizer guarantee.

The linear model demonstration assumes fully observed predictor matrix X and t-distributed response errors. Expected weighted XX, XY and YY statistics feed weighted regression and scatter, followed by observed-likelihood fitting of nu. Inverses need rank conditions; this demonstration does not justify unmodeled missing predictors.

limitations.note: Missingness is explicitly assumed ignorable. Multiple stationary points and narrow high-likelihood spikes can arise, particularly with small or unknown degrees of freedom; a mode need not summarize posterior mass. Optimization is not posterior sampling or a guarantee of meaningful clinical inference.

An artificial bivariate incomplete-data example uses common specified starts and a1e-5 component tolerance; its table compares7061 EM iterations,7053 multicycle ECM and130 ECME, with per-iteration cost0.26,0.26,1.92 seconds. These are source-reported historical context, not reproduced or general performance assertions. Figure1 caption is visible but its plotting region is blank in the inspected PDF render; no curve shape was inspected.

A historical34-male-patient creatinine dataset includes missing weight/serum-creatinine values. A joint t model of transformed response AND predictors handles those missing covariates, unlike the fully observed-X regression derivation. Case-deletion and normal-limit fits are historical illustrations, not clinical validation. Table5 labels cumulative distribution values as p-values; do not interpret them as ordinary upper-tail significance probabilities.

pxem.abstract_interpretation: Parameter expansion adds identifiable complete-data parameters while preserving the observed-data family, then fits and reduces the expanded model. The paper relates this to covariance adjustment and supplies several examples. The conditional local-rate theorem is narrower than an unconditional computational speed guarantee.

mechanism.note: Expanded complete-data density pX(ycom|theta_star,alpha) must recover the original at alpha0 and induce exactly the original observed-data family through an explicit reduction R. Each iteration embeds (theta_t,alpha0), computes expanded conditional sufficient moments, maximizes expanded Q, reduces to theta_new, and reembeds with alpha reset. Merely adding free observed-model parameters is not PX-EM. The auxiliary parameter is not estimated as an independently identified observed parameter.

Proper expanded EM plus likelihood-preserving reduction yields nondecreasing observed likelihood; bounded likelihood values converge. Stationary or local-maximum parameter convergence needs further EM regularity, not just that inequality.

Rate comparison linearizes at an MLE, assumes convergence and existence of the stated derivatives/inverses, with positive complete-data information. Observed information has zero auxiliary blocks in (theta,alpha) coordinates. Block inversion gives V_theta_theta >= original complete-data inverse; hence the slowest local linear speed is at least as large as the parent's. The paper calls this global rate, meaning the extremal eigenvalue across parameter directions near the fixed point, not global convergence from arbitrary starts. Equality is possible; CPU time and finite iterations are not ordered by this theorem.

For multivariate t with fixed positive nu, expected latent weights are (nu+p)/(nu+Mahalanobis). Parent EM updates scatter with denominator N. Expand gamma weight mean to alpha, estimate alpha=sum weights/N and reduce scatter Psi_star/alpha. Resulting scatter denominator is sum weights. Alpha resets to1. The reduction preserves the marginal t law; generic arbitrary renormalization is not justified by a convenient speed claim.

The covariance-adjustment expression is locally approximate in general. In the explicit scalar normal model, y|z~N(z,1), z~N(theta,sigma2) with known positive sigma2, EM contracts error by1/(1+sigma2). Expanding y|z~N(z+alpha,1), reducing theta_star+alpha, gives theta_new=y in one exact update. The boundary sigma2=0 is outside the stated positive-variance setup.

Random-effects expansion uses a matrix alpha in the linear predictor and reduces random-effect covariance to alpha Psi_star alpha transpose. First and second conditional moments enter regression sufficient statistics. Table1 compares iterations at one dataset per noise variance with explicit starts and tolerance; it is not a universal time/quality benchmark.

Factor analysis expands latent covariance from I to alpha, estimates alpha from conditional second moments, and absorbs a square root into loadings so beta beta transpose equals beta_star alpha beta_star transpose. The expanded family leaves the observed covariance intact. Square-root orientation must satisfy that equality explicitly; do not copy ambiguous SWEEP indexing as an algorithm.

Probit expansion frees latent Gaussian variance alpha squared and reduces coefficients theta_star/alpha for positive alpha. Correct truncated first and second moments are required. The printed second-moment equation fails a basic zero-linear-predictor check, recorded below; do not assert it. Historical kyphosis and simulated examples are not reproduced.

The Poisson imaging illustration splits signal and background latent counts, activates a background split parameter and reduces theta_star+alpha-a0. Parameter nonnegativity and r_i-k_i*a0>=0 constrain the construction. The printed conditional expectation for U has a numerator inconsistent with its Poisson mean, recorded below.
